title: Architecture and Trust Boundaries
---

# Architecture and Trust Boundaries

Guardrails ADR separates untrusted endpoint telemetry, customer tenant administration, and multi-tenant infrastructure operations across strict crate layers (`contracts/architecture.toml`) and network/IPC boundaries.

## Split Console and Operator Planes

`grdr-server` refuses to start if `--bind` and `--operator-bind` resolve to the same socket address:

- **Tenant Console Plane (`--bind`):** Hosts customer Web UI (`--web-dir`) and Connect/Protobuf RPC services (`grdr.api.overview.v1alpha1.OverviewService`, `InventoryService`, `VerdictService`, `PolicyService`, `SessionService`, `UserService`, `ResponseService`, and `SurfaceService`).
- **Operator Plane (`--operator-bind`):** Hosts isolated Operator UI (`--operator-web-dir`), `grdr.api.operator.v1alpha1.OperatorService` with explicit impersonation and break-glass receipts, plus scoped read-only `OverviewService` and `ResponseService` audit endpoints under separate bearer credentials (`--operator-token`).

## OS Peer-Authenticated Endpoint IPC

`grdr-daemon` exposes zero HTTP or TCP listeners. Local callers connect over OS peer-authenticated IPC (`Unix domain sockets` on Linux/macOS or named pipes on Windows) with process identity validation enforced before handling decisions or configuration reads.

## Dynamic Manifest-Driven Catalogue

Agent harnesses, detection fingerprints, compliance controls, and integrations are declared in signed packs and TOML/JSON/YAML manifests rather than static compiled enumerations. Supporting new agents or integrations requires no core engine recompilation.

## Assurance Levels (`AL0` to `AL4`)

Endpoints report an explicit **Assurance level** (`AL0` discovery-only through `AL4` signed OS/kernel enforcement with verified binary floor) derived from observed sensor, hook, and hardware key attestation evidence.

# Port Contracts and Workspace Layers

All storage, message bus, blob store, relational metadata, job journal, sandbox, and sensor adapters live behind explicit traits in `crates/grdr-ports`.

## Layer Ordering (`contracts/architecture.toml`)

- **Layer 0 (Contracts & Wire):** `grdr-proto`, `grdr-schema`.
- **Layer 1 (Pure Core, Crypto & FFI):** `grdr-compat`, `grdr-core`, `grdr-crypto`, `grdr-fastpath`, `grdr-fastpath-ffi`, `grdr-ffi`, `grdr-intel`, `grdr-llm-proto`, `grdr-mcp-proto`, `grdr-model`, `grdr-review`, `grdr-wasm`.
- **Layer 2 (Ports & Messaging):** `grdr-messages`, `grdr-ports`, `grdr-ports-testkit`, `grdr-strings`, `grdr-wire`.
- **Layer 3 (Adapters & Operations):** `grdr-agents`, `grdr-blob`, `grdr-broker`, `grdr-bus-log`, `grdr-bus-nats`, `grdr-comply`, `grdr-export`, `grdr-identity`, `grdr-integrations`, `grdr-ipc-os`, `grdr-jobs`, `grdr-lake`, `grdr-os-clock`, `grdr-os-service`, `grdr-peer-os`, `grdr-rel-postgres`, `grdr-rel-sqlite`, `grdr-saas`, `grdr-sandbox-engine`, `grdr-sensor-linux`, `grdr-sensor-macos`, `grdr-sensor-windows`, `grdr-store-local`, `grdr-ui-model`, `grdr-update`.
- **Layer 4 (Executables under `programs/`):** `grdr`, `grdr-acp`, `grdr-approve`, `grdr-daemon`, `grdr-engine`, `grdr-hook`, `grdr-infer`, `grdr-interface-gen`, `grdr-mcp`, `grdr-proxy`, `grdr-run`, `grdr-server`, `grdr-tray`, `grdr-updater`, `grdr-uplink`.
- **Tooling (`tools/`):** `grdr-conformance`, `grdr-policy-ref`, `grdr-schema-lint`.

## Sole Cryptography Boundary

`grdr-crypto` is the sole crate permitted to invoke Ed25519, SHA-256, HMAC, or ChaCha20-Poly1305 primitives directly. Higher layers (`grdr-saas`, `grdr-lake`, `grdr-server`) call `grdr-crypto` helpers exclusively.

See [Adding a Port Adapter](../../extending/adding-a-port-adapter.md) for conformance harness requirements (`grdr-ports-testkit`).

title: Configure Agent Hooks and MCP Proxy

# Configure Agent Hooks and MCP Proxy

Guardrails ADR enforces policies synchronously at tool boundaries using `grdr-hook` and `grdr mcp-proxy`. Both components fail closed whenever local policy evaluation cannot complete within the latency watchdog budget.

## Preview and Install Harness Hooks

Inspect current hook status without touching local settings files:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- hook status --agent claude-code
cargo run -p grdr -- hook install --agent claude-code
```

Without `--apply`, `grdr hook install` previews the exact configuration diff and backup path. Pass `--apply` only when you want to write the backup journal and install the hook.

To revert cleanly from the backup journal:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- hook uninstall --agent claude-code
```

## Wrap Stdio MCP Servers with `grdr mcp-proxy`

Wrap any stdio JSON-RPC MCP server so every `tools/call` invocation passes local policy checks and tool-pinning verification:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- mcp-proxy --server-name filesystem --agent claude-code -- your-mcp-server-binary
```

Replace the trailing command with your MCP server executable and arguments. If tool schemas drift from pinned manifests, `grdr mcp-proxy` blocks execution and writes a signed receipt.

## Verify Hash-Chained Local Receipts

Verify local JSONL receipt integrity after running hook or MCP evaluations:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- audit verify --json
```

title: Manage Policy Packs and Cedar Rules

# Manage Policy Packs and Cedar Rules

Policy evaluation in Guardrails ADR runs Cedar authorization checks and signed content packs compiled down to the endpoint daemon floor cache.

## Evaluation Modes

Every policy rule produces one of four Guardrails modes and verdicts:

- `Off`: rule disabled in the current assignment.
- `Watch`: record findings and telemetry receipts without blocking execution.
- `Ask`: require bounded step-up `Grant` approval from Console or Desktop before allowing the action.
- `Block`: deny immediately at hook or OS sensor boundary and emit a block notice receipt.

## Signed Floor Compilation

The endpoint daemon (`grdr-daemon`) compiles active policy packs into an Ed25519-verified binary floor cache. If the server uplink disconnects or restarts, local hook evaluation continues offline against the pinned binary floor cache.

## Verifying Pack Conformance

Always run workspace checks after editing packs or Cedar contracts:

```powershell
cargo test --workspace --locked
node scripts/check-architecture.mjs
```

See [Adding a Rule or Pack](../../extending/adding-a-rule-or-pack.md) for pack authoring fixtures and negative test requirements.

title: Releases, Support Windows, and Upgrades

# Releases, Support Windows, and Upgrades

Release cadence, upgrade hops, deprecations, and platform support tiers are defined machine-readably in:

- `contracts/support.toml` (supported OSes, architectures, databases, Kubernetes `1.35..1.37`, sensor skew `+1` / `-2`)
- `lifecycle.toml` (release lines, cadence, deprecation notice windows)
- `contracts/upgrade-path.json` (SemVer series hop and rollback policy matrix)
- `upgrade-path.json` (lifecycle command, preflight/migrate invocations, and runbook bindings)
- `docs/lifecycle/deprecations.toml` and `docs/lifecycle/known-issues.toml`

## Upgrade Constraints

- Monthly release cadence supporting up to `2` minor versions behind on active lines.
- Maximum direct upgrade jump: `2` minor versions (`max_upgrade_minor_hop = 2`).
- Rollback window: `1` minor version (`rollback_window_minors = 1`).
- Sensor skew tolerance: endpoints may lag up to `2` minor versions behind `grdr-server` or lead by `1` minor version.
- Breaking removals follow a minimum notice floor of `2` releases and `180` days once a surface enters stable GA compatibility.

## Pre-Release Surface Cleanup

Pre-release prototype REST JSON endpoints and loopback daemon HTTP ports were removed prior to `v0.1.0` in favor of typed Connect/Protobuf services and OS peer-authenticated IPC (`docs/lifecycle/deprecations.toml`).

title: Hosted SaaS Cells, Portability, and Billing
---

# Hosted SaaS Cells, Portability, and Billing

Multi-tenant hosted operations are implemented in `crates/grdr-saas`.

## 4096-Bucket Regional Cell Sharding

- Devices hash via SHA-256 into deterministic shard buckets across `[0, 4096)`.
- Each cell owns a contiguous bucket range and capacity vector tracking CPU, active sessions, storage, and write IOPS utilization.
- New tenant placements enforce regional residency pinning (`GRDR-SAAS-0003`) and trigger splits at the 70% utilization soft cap (`docs/ops/bounds.toml` and `contracts/limits.toml`) leaving 20% emergency headroom.
- Splitting a hot cell halves `[start, end)` at the midpoint (`[0, 2048)` and `[2048, 4096)`) and reassigns matching organisations cleanly without gaps or overlapping ownership.

## Lossless Organisation Portability

Organisations can migrate between hosted cells or export cleanly to self-hosted clusters:

- Signed migration bundles carry `lake/` Parquet/blob artifacts, `audit/` hash-chained logs, active revocation IDs, and the current kill-switch epoch under strict single-organisation tenant scoping (`GRDR-SAAS-0004` rejects cross-tenant or delegated exports/imports).
- Every payload blob matches its declared manifest byte length and SHA-256 digest (`GRDR-SAAS-0005` rejects tampering or unmanifested blobs), and imports enforce monotonic watermark checks so old bundles cannot downgrade security state.
- Endpoints receive Ed25519-signed cell redirect receipts checked against minimum supported client SemVer requirements and HTTPS endpoint validation.

## Usage Ledger, Billing, and Dunning Safety

- The usage ledger scopes idempotency keys strictly per organisation and drops stale telemetry older than the 35-day late-usage window (`GRDR-SAAS-0006`).
- Monthly statements are Ed25519-signed and emitted uniformly across statement file, Stripe Meter, and Kill Bill adapters.
- Billing reconciliation blocks invoice issuance (`GRDR-SAAS-0007`) whenever any billed metric deviates beyond policy tolerance (`0%` exact line check or `10 bps` drift tolerance) or fails price/subtotal validation.
- Local endpoint enforcement remains active throughout `14`-day payment retry, past-due, and `60`-day suspended dunning states so endpoints never lose local protection while billing resolves.

title: Server Storage Profiles and Migrations
---

# Server Storage Profiles and Migrations

`grdr-server` supports three storage topologies (`--profile`):

| Profile | Relational Store | Event Bus Adapter | Object Store | Primary Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `embedded` | SQLite (`grdr-rel-sqlite`) | Relational WAL log (`grdr-bus-log` / `sqlite-log` in `contracts/support.toml`) | Local filesystem | Single-node self-hosted and developer setups |
| `ha` | PostgreSQL 18 (`grdr-rel-postgres`) | Relational WAL log (`grdr-bus-log` / `postgresql-log` in `contracts/support.toml`) | Local or S3-compatible object store | High-availability multi-replica team clusters |
| `distributed` | PostgreSQL 18 (`grdr-rel-postgres`) | NATS JetStream (`grdr-bus-nats` / `2.15.2`) | AWS S3, GCS, Azure Blob, SeaweedFS, or Ceph RGW | Large enterprise fleets and regional SaaS cells |

## Preflight Verification

Run preflight checks before starting or upgrading a deployment profile:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- server preflight --profile ha --strict --json
```

Preflight validates disk headroom, PostgreSQL/NATS connectivity where configured, object-store readiness, and sensor skew constraints (`-2` / `+1` minor versions per `contracts/support.toml`).

## Schema Migrations

Preview and execute deterministic, lock-fenced schema and object migrations prior to rolling traffic:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- server migrate --from-data-dir ./grdr-data --target-bucket-dir ./grdr-object-store --dry-run
cargo run -p grdr -- server migrate --from-data-dir ./grdr-data --target-bucket-dir ./grdr-object-store
```

Consult [RB-02 Upgrade and Rollback](../../runbooks/RB-02-release-upgrade-rollback.md) before hopping minor versions.

# Diagnostics, Support Bundles, and Offline Verification

## Endpoint Diagnostics (`grdr doctor`)

Run non-destructive health and connectivity checks on an endpoint:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- doctor
```

Each diagnostic check prints structured `GRDR-<AREA>-<NNNN>` remediation hints pointing to relevant sections in this documentation bundle.

## Redacted Support Bundles

Collect redacted logs, configuration summaries, and state watermarks for troubleshooting without exposing prompt payloads or local credentials:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- support-bundle
```

Always inspect the preview archive before sharing diagnostics outside your trust boundary.

## Air-Gapped Deployments (`grdr airgap`)

Air-gapped environments pack signed policy packs, CLI/daemon binaries, and offline documentation HTML from `website/build/` so operators and endpoints retain local docs search (Pagefind) without external network access.

After every rollout or cell drill, record completion against [Fleet Verification Checklist](../../runbooks/FLEET-VERIFY.md).

# Quickstart

Run Guardrails ADR locally on Windows, macOS, or Linux in under five minutes.

## 1. Build the Console and Operator Frontends

```powershell
pnpm --dir web install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir web run build
```

This builds the customer Console in `web/dist/` and the isolated Operator interface in `web/dist-operator/`.

## 2. Start `grdr-server`

Launch the split control-plane host with distinct Console (`--bind`) and Operator (`--operator-bind`) socket bindings:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr-server -- --bind 127.0.0.1:8787 --operator-bind 127.0.0.1:8788 --web-dir web/dist --operator-web-dir web/dist-operator --demo-seed --data-dir ./grdr-data
```

- Customer Console and Connect RPC API (`grdr.api.*`): `http://127.0.0.1:8787/`
- Isolated Operator UI and Operator Connect RPC (`grdr.api.operator.v1alpha1.OperatorService`): `http://127.0.0.1:8788/`

## 3. Run Endpoint Discovery and Daemon Self-Test

Verify the OS peer-authenticated IPC supervisor (`grdr-daemon`) without modifying host configuration:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr-daemon -- --self-test
```

Discover installed AI coding harnesses and MCP servers from local declarative manifests:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- scan
cargo run -p grdr -- doctor
```

## 4. Evaluate Actions and Hook Payloads

Check how active Essentials rules evaluate a sensitive configuration write:

```powershell
cargo run -p grdr -- check --action file.write --target .claude/settings.json
```

Test `grdr-hook` directly via stdin JSON:

```powershell
'{"session_id":"s1","tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":".claude/settings.json"}}' | cargo run -p grdr-hook
```

## Next Steps

- [Configure Hooks and MCP Proxy](../how-to/configure-hooks-and-mcp.md)
- [Server Storage Profiles and Preflight](../operate/server-profiles.md)

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/FLEET-VERIFY.md sha256:6eebb304adb854231d1bf3eb06ed99e9afc0df585363dcc44b2d297bebb23cc2 -->
# Fleet Verification Checklist (`GRDR-VERIFY-<YYYY-MM-DD>`)

Execute all three verification tracks after any regional failover drill, storage migration, or minor release rollout. Save the completed record as `GRDR-VERIFY-YYYY-MM-DD` attached to the change ticket.

## Track 1: Control Planes and Storage Integrity

- [ ] `grdr server preflight --profile <embedded|ha|distributed> --strict` exits `0` against the target deployment profile.
- [ ] `--bind` (Console/API) and `--operator-bind` (Operator plane) resolve to distinct socket addresses.
- [ ] `OperatorService` RPCs on `--operator-bind` require separate `--operator-token` credentials and emit immutable impersonation receipts.
- [ ] Lake and relational checksums pass after backup restore within `RPO <= 5m` and `RTO < 4h`.

## Track 2: Endpoint IPC, Fastpath, and Receipts

- [ ] `grdr-daemon --self-test` exits `0` with zero TCP/HTTP listeners bound.
- [ ] `grdr doctor` reports healthy OS peer-authenticated IPC and signed floor cache verification.
- [ ] `grdr check --action file.write --target .claude/settings.json` fails closed (`Block`) within latency SLO.
- [ ] `grdr audit verify --json` verifies hash-chained JSONL receipts without continuity breaks.

## Track 3: SaaS Cells, Reconciliation, and Security Watchers

- [ ] Contiguous shard bucket ownership across all active regional cells covers `[0, 4096)` cleanly with zero overlap or utilization above 70%.
- [ ] Sample organisation migration bundle export/import roundtrip succeeds and preserves active revocation grants and `kill_switch_epoch`.
- [ ] Monthly billing statement reconciliation holds `0%` variance (`<= 10 bps` drift tolerance) across statement file, Stripe, and Kill Bill adapters.
- [ ] Change freeze and operational bounds (`<= 25%` blast radius, `1` concurrent region) verified cleanly.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-01-cell-restore-and-dr.md sha256:920428a12e431d48055d74193ec2baa091cef3475ccdd79252efc276b5f71951 -->
---
id: RB-01
actor: sre-oncall
rto: 4h
rpo: 5m
---

# RB-01: Cell Backup Restore and Disaster Recovery

## Diagnosis

1. Confirm cell outage or unrecoverable storage corruption via health metrics and SLO burn alerts (`docs/ops/slo-rules.yaml`).
2. Verify latest continuous backup snapshot timestamp in the regional object store (`aws-s3`, `gcs`, `azure-blob`, `seaweedfs-4.53`, or `ceph-rgw`) meets `RPO <= 5m`.
3. Confirm standby compute capacity exists in the tenant's pinned region (`required_region`) to preserve data locality.

## Actions

1. Record an incident ticket and runbook operator provenance (`blast_radius_pct <= 25`, `max_concurrent_regions = 1`, `30`-minute regional cooldown).
2. Restore PostgreSQL 18 WAL PITR snapshot into the replacement cell database (`RB-06`).
3. Hydrate immutable `lake/` Parquet batches and `audit/` receipt segments from the regional object store.
4. Run `grdr server preflight --profile ha --strict --json` against the restored cell configuration, verifying distinct `--bind` and `--operator-bind`.
5. Register the restored cell endpoint in the control-plane cell router and clear draining state only after checksum parity passes.

## Verification

- Compare restored `lake_watermark` and `audit_watermark` against pre-incident checkpoints.
- Execute Track 1 and Track 2 of [FLEET-VERIFY.md](FLEET-VERIFY.md) inside the `4h` RTO window.

## Rollback

If restored WAL or lake segments fail digest checks, place the replacement cell into read-only mode, retain primary quarantine evidence, and restore from the prior clean snapshot.

## Escalation

Page Security On-Call (`RB-07`) immediately if checksum mismatches suggest tampering rather than crash recovery.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-02-release-upgrade-rollback.md sha256:40ef6bc1dd4fa4eb4979a6702f337c8bb14d8873bcd2deae790cef671942de34 -->

id: RB-02
actor: release-manager

# RB-02: Release Upgrade and Minor Rollback

## Diagnosis

1. Inspect `lifecycle.toml` and `upgrade-path.json` for approved hop paths (`max_upgrade_minor_hop = 2`, `rollback_window_minors = 1`).
2. Check active endpoint versions against sensor skew policy (`2` minors behind to `1` minor ahead per `contracts/support.toml`).

## Actions

1. Execute `grdr server preflight --profile ha --strict --json` on the target cluster.
2. When schema revision changes, execute `grdr server migrate --from-data-dir <PATH> --target-bucket-dir <PATH> --dry-run` followed by live cutover prior to shifting control-plane traffic.
3. Roll server deployments canary-first under `docs/ops/bounds.toml` concurrency caps (`1` region at a time), monitoring Connect RPC error rates.

## Verification

- Verify `grdr doctor` and `grdr server preflight --profile ha --strict` pass on upgraded nodes.
- Verify endpoint hooks continue enforcing the signed local floor cache without fallback disruptions.

## Rollback

If error rates or p99 decision latency exceed SLO thresholds, roll server binaries back within `1` minor version (`rollback_window_minors = 1`) after pausing irreversible migrations.

## Escalation

Escalate to Platform Architecture if a schema compatibility bump forces emergency protocol negotiation changes.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-03-org-cell-migration-and-export.md sha256:7459cc0d2ccca08287e1c133e922be823364cda998057769abcbd36341463491 -->
---
id: RB-03
actor: saas-ops
rto: 1h
rpo: 0m
---

# RB-03: Organisation Cell Migration and Self-Hosted Export

## Diagnosis

1. Confirm the organisation's target cell or self-hosted export request matches pinned data residency and non-delegated single-tenant context ownership.
2. Verify all endpoints meet the minimum supported agent version specified in the migration manifest.

## Actions

1. Place source placement into drain mode and open the dual-write telemetry catch-up window.
2. Freeze tenant mutations briefly (`Frozen` migration stage) and export an Ed25519-signed organisation migration bundle containing `lake/`, `audit/`, revoked grant IDs, and the active `kill_switch_epoch`.
3. Import the bundle under target tenant verification, checking manifest SHA-256 digests, blob lengths, and monotonic watermark baselines.
4. Commit placement cutover and issue Ed25519-signed device redirect receipts (`https://` endpoint verified) to active endpoints.

## Verification

- Confirm restored file count matches source manifest count and `kill_switch_epoch` / revoked grant IDs match identically.
- Verify cross-tenant or delegated bundle attempts fail cleanly with `GRDR-SAAS-0004`.

## Rollback

Before device redirect receipts expire, revert target drain state and direct endpoints back to the source cell while holding target quarantine data read-only.

## Escalation

Escalate to Security On-Call on any `GRDR-SAAS-0005` signature mismatch or manifest checksum error.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-04-cell-split-and-rebalance.md sha256:cc7b9b9e8e05906ff3ee85f53e79b506d0662da689ce1a32502d31f60f6d4fe3 -->
---
id: RB-04
actor: saas-ops
rto: 45m
rpo: 0m
---

# RB-04: Cell Shard Split and Capacity Rebalance

## Diagnosis

1. Alert fires when any capacity dimension (CPU, active sessions, storage, write IOPS) hits the 70% cell soft cap configured in `docs/ops/bounds.toml` and `contracts/limits.toml`.
2. Confirm the active target cell owns at least two contiguous shard buckets.

## Actions

1. Provision an empty active cell endpoint in the same region with healthy capacity headroom (`< 70%`).
2. Trigger a regional cell shard split, halving `[start, end)` cleanly at the midpoint with zero bucket gap or overlap and proportional capacity allocation.
3. Drain and migrate reassigned organisations falling into the upper half range (`RB-03`).

## Verification

- Verify source and new cell utilizations both fall well below `70%` leaving `>= 20%` emergency reserve.
- Verify full coverage of `[0, 4096)` across regional cells with zero overlap.

## Rollback

Mark the newly provisioned cell as draining, move reassigned orgs back to the source cell only after reducing tenant load, or provision larger compute backing on both halves.

## Escalation

Escalate to SRE Lead if a single hot organisation drives `> 70%` utilization on a minimal bucket range (`dedicated cell` trigger).

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-05-nats-jetstream-recovery.md sha256:202572689d695316b5214a1ad4e2000f3c86389b48e257dc15e9c03d76567f2d -->
---
id: RB-05
actor: sre-oncall
rto: 30m
rpo: 0m
---

# RB-05: NATS JetStream Stream and Consumer Recovery

## Diagnosis

1. Triggered when `--profile distributed` event ingest lag breaches SLO thresholds or a JetStream quorum member loses raft consensus.
2. Inspect `grdr-bus-nats` stream state, consumer ACK pending counts, and storage volume free space.

## Actions

1. Verify at least two of three JetStream RAFT peers remain healthy; replace failed PVC/peer node before shrinking replication factor.
2. If backlog spikes due to stalled workers, scale consumer replicas up within `bounds.toml` rate limits rather than purging durable streams.
3. Replay unacknowledged ingest sequences from durable stream checkpoints; idempotency keys deduplicate retried records safely.

## Verification

- Confirm consumer lag drains to nominal baseline and no sequence gaps appear in `lake/` flush checkpoints.

## Rollback

Switch degraded workers off traffic while preserving JetStream storage volumes intact until raft leader quorum stabilizes.

## Escalation

Engage Platform Storage team if quorum loss exceeds two peers (`RPO` assessment against object-store lake backups required).

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-06-postgres-failover-and-pitr.md sha256:5ad12ae8002e56048a703c692167af53f3ac5cda4386750f060619d99402816b -->
---
id: RB-06
actor: sre-oncall
rto: 30m
rpo: 5m
---

# RB-06: PostgreSQL 18 Failover and Point-in-Time Recovery

## Diagnosis

1. Triggered on primary database unavailability, replication slot lag breach, or fenced write failure in `--profile ha` / `distributed`.
2. Verify CloudNativePG (`cnpg`) cluster health, WAL archive continuity, and standby sync state.

## Actions

1. Promote synchronous standby when primary is dead and confirm fencing token epoch increments (`FencingToken`).
2. For logical corruption or accidental DDL, initialize a clean PostgreSQL 18 cluster from WAL archive up to target PITR timestamp immediately prior to fault.
3. Run `grdr server preflight --profile ha --strict --postgres-dsn <DSN> --json` before directing `grdr-server` connection pools to the promoted cluster.

## Verification

- Confirm `grdr server preflight --profile ha --strict` passes and Connect/Protobuf read/write RPCs return healthy latencies.

## Rollback

Retain fenced old primary read-only for forensic diffing; never reattach diverged primaries without pg_rewind validation or fresh basebackup.

## Escalation

Escalate to Security On-Call (`RB-07`) if audit table rows or tenant fencing records show unexpected divergence.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-07-key-rotation-and-custody.md sha256:87c9d26c99a20312d2f56e73dfd93d0457d9986d221083b8af298d3e6cdde169 -->
---
id: RB-07
actor: security-oncall
rto: 1h
rpo: 0m
---

# RB-07: Key Rotation, Custody Ceremony, and Compromise Yank

## Diagnosis

1. Triggered on suspected Ed25519 key exposure, scheduled root/signing rotation, or foreign artefact signature discovery.
2. Identify key scope (`TUF root`, `pack signer`, `route ticket`, or `device identity`) and verify Rekor transparency entries (`RB-12`).

## Actions

1. Add replacement Ed25519 verifying key to pinned trust stores prior to removing the retiring key (overlap window).
2. On active key compromise, revoke affected releases immediately (`TUF` expiry bump), bump `kill_switch_epoch` where required, and invoke the yank advisory template (`docs/ops/security-advisories/vex-csaf-template.json`).
3. Re-sign active floor packs and route tickets exclusively using clean custody keys (`grdr-crypto`).

## Verification

- Confirm `grdr audit verify --json` and bundle signature verification succeed under the rotated public key and fail closed against revoked signatures (`GRDR-SAAS-0005`).

## Rollback

Never un-revoke a compromised key; rotate forward cleanly with fresh generated key material.

## Escalation

Notify Incident Commander and Steward Owner per repository root `SECURITY.md` within 15 minutes of confirmed key compromise.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-08-kill-switch-and-emergency-contain.md sha256:e01660567a2cea5226b40994d8fb74626bdadff7e45fccadc5248b4ca271ede9 -->
---
id: RB-08
actor: incident-commander
rto: 15m
rpo: 0m
---

# RB-08: Emergency Kill Switch and Scoped Containment

## Diagnosis

1. Confirm active misuse or high-severity containment signal in Console Respond (`grdr.api.response.v1alpha1.ResponseService`) or the Operator plane (`grdr.api.operator.v1alpha1.OperatorService`).
2. Identify exact scope (single agent session, single device, or tenant org) before escalating containment scope.

## Actions

1. Issue bounded kill-switch activation via Response RPC (`KillSwitchState`), verifying epoch increment (`kill_switch_epoch`) in endpoint receipts.
2. Confirm hook and MCP proxy fail closed (`Block`) across targeted sessions.
3. Preserve forensic audit chains and collect a support bundle (`grdr support-bundle`) prior to clearing containment state.

## Verification

- Verify `grdr status` reflects active isolation epoch and no targeted tool execution bypasses local enforcement.

## Rollback

Complete authenticated step-up approval in the Console or Desktop approval prompt and record a documented clearance reason before lifting kill switch.

## Escalation

Engage Trust & Safety and Customer Security Contact when cross-host lateral abuse is observed.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-09-billing-reconciliation-halt.md sha256:a5157b05d0296c050cb66eba8c398e3534e6dcbbc05f1beb879a2597e3c1c308 -->
---
id: RB-09
actor: billing-ops
rto: 2h
rpo: 0m
---

# RB-09: Billing Reconciliation Halt and Usage Replay

## Diagnosis

1. Triggered when billing reconciliation returns `GRDR-SAAS-0007` (variance > `0%` exact line check, duplicate invoice line identifiers, unit-price mismatch, subtotal mismatch, or > `10 bps` meter drift).
2. Inspect the signed monthly usage statement digest and compare against raw usage ledger records per organisation and billing period.

## Actions

1. Halt automated invoice finalization for the affected billing period and `org_id`.
2. Replay late-arriving samples strictly inside the `35`-day late-usage window (`contracts/limits.toml`) using per-organisation, hour/day-bucketed idempotency keys so retries cannot double-bill.
3. Recompute the signed monthly usage statement and re-run per-metric parity across statement file, Stripe Meter, and Kill Bill adapters.

## Verification

- Confirm strict zero-variance reconciliation passes with `drift_bps == 0` across all billed metrics (`active_endpoints`, `ephemeral_sensor_hours`, `daily_active_endpoint_days`, `over_retention_gb_days`).

## Rollback

Void unissued draft invoices matching stale idempotency keys rather than patching ledger figures manually.

## Escalation

Escalate to Finance Lead and SaaS Engineering Lead if drift stems from clock skew exceeding `35` days (`GRDR-SAAS-0006`).

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-10-slo-burn-rate-incident.md sha256:6177f97a27376e84c4c1a58c488b9f54673a7fb3d014530d8d7ada8ffb3158a1 -->
---
id: RB-10
actor: sre-oncall
rto: 15m
rpo: 5m
---

# RB-10: SLO Error-Budget Burn Rate Incident

## Diagnosis

1. Page triggers on `docs/ops/slo-rules.yaml` multi-window fast-burn rules (`14.4x` over 1h or `6x` over 6h) for Connect RPC ingest, decision fastpath, or fleet sync.
2. Correlate burn spike with recent automated runbook maintenance steps, deploys, or traffic surges.

## Actions

1. Declare a change freeze window blocking non-emergency rollouts (`docs/ops/bounds.toml`).
2. Route around unhealthy cells (`RB-04` / `RB-01`) or roll back recent minor rollout (`RB-02`).
3. Verify offline local `grdr-daemon` / `grdr-hook` binary floor cache continues protecting endpoints with zero disruption.

## Verification

- Error-budget burn falls below `1x` across a clean 30-minute recovery window before lifting change freeze.

## Rollback

Keep change freeze active until post-incident corrective action is tracked.

## Escalation

Page Incident Commander (`RB-08`) if fast-burn spans more than one regional cell simultaneously.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-11-tenant-abuse-dunning-erasure.md sha256:db3ef9d4693ad2d4b053632efdc879de98921854f4cea71ef15dd786033f2c92 -->
---
id: RB-11
actor: trust-safety
rto: 4h
rpo: 0m
---

# RB-11: Tenant Dunning, Suspension, and Legal-Hold Erasure

## Diagnosis

1. Triggered by billing invoice delinquency (`PastDue` through `14`-day retry window to `Suspended` through `60`-day grace), abuse report, or contractual offboarding erasure request.
2. Verify active legal hold status before mutating tenant keys or encrypted blobs.

## Actions

1. Under payment delinquency, preserve active local endpoint enforcement so endpoints never silently drop protection while billing resolves.
2. Provide self-hosted migration export (`RB-03`) prior to locking hosted portals.
3. For approved offboarding with no legal hold active, schedule pending erasure (`30`-day cancellation window from `contracts/limits.toml`) and finalize cryptographic key destruction only after the deadline passes.

## Verification

- Confirm held tenants and non-elapsed erasure deadlines reject key purge (`GRDR-SAAS-0008`), and completed erasures verify destroyed session content keys.

## Rollback

While pending erasure inside the `30`-day cancellation window, customer authorization or newly raised legal hold cancels scheduled purge cleanly; billing delinquency transitions cannot override an already pending or completed erasure.

## Escalation

Escalate immediately to Legal Counsel (`docs/legal/counsel-register.yaml`) if conflicting regulatory retention and erasure demands occur.

<!-- source: docs/runbooks/RB-12-sigstore-and-supply-chain-alert.md sha256:77526625b3e12be567fb49a9033e10ef4e8f53282067db097509383726bc5551 -->
---
id: RB-12
actor: security-oncall
rto: 1h
rpo: 0m
---

# RB-12: Sigstore Transparency Log and Supply-Chain Alert

## Diagnosis

1. Triggered within 1 hour when Rekor transparency monitoring or crates/npm namespace checks detect an unexpected signature, OIDC issuer mismatch, or untrusted provenance digest.
2. Inspect `security/trust-core.paths`, release workflows, and Sigstore bundle signatures for the flagged artifact.

## Actions

1. Pause downstream release promotion and TUF metadata publication immediately.
2. Compare suspect binary hash against reproducible builder digest (`verify-artefact` / SLSA provenance).
3. If unauthorized signing is confirmed, execute key revocation and yank (`RB-07`) and populate `docs/ops/security-advisories/vex-csaf-template.json`.

## Verification

- Verify all published release manifests validate strictly against expected repository workflow OIDC claims and clean `cargo deny --config security/deny.toml check` output.

## Rollback

Do not re-enable automated release tags until root cause and signer credential hygiene are independently verified.

## Escalation

Escalate to Steward Owner and external coordinated disclosure list per repository root `SECURITY.md`.

<!-- source: docs/extending/adding-a-port-adapter.md sha256:883cbec7d475a51128f1c4a57dd5963dabff65f81cb29caa742468b0ec2e2280 -->
# Adding a Port Adapter

Storage, message bus, blob store, job journal, sandbox, and OS sensor backends implement stable traits declared in `crates/grdr-ports` (`Layer 2`) inside dedicated `Layer 3` crates.

## Requirements

1. Declare `[package.metadata.grdr]` (`layer = 3`, `privilege = "none"` or audited trust-core tier, `surface = "internal"`, `renders = "none"`) in the adapter `Cargo.toml`.
2. Register the crate in `contracts/architecture.toml` and all error codes (`GRDR-<AREA>-<NNNN>`) in `contracts/codes/registry.toml`.
3. Depend on `grdr-crypto` instead of adding external cryptographic crates.
4. Pass the full conformance suite exported by `crates/grdr-ports-testkit` (`assert_blob_port_contract`, `assert_job_port_contract`, `assert_events_port_contract`, `assert_bus_port_contract`, `assert_relational_store_contract`).
5. Validate SPDX licence headers (`scripts/licence-lint.mjs`), dependency allow-list (`cargo deny --config security/deny.toml check`), and architecture rules (`node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`).

<!-- source: docs/extending/adding-a-rule-or-pack.md sha256:7792d92e190ca86aa725372a510227c5e81b36b34172ffa74b31b75cc58f053a -->
# Adding a Rule or Policy Pack

Policy rules and Essentials baselines evaluate typed actions against Cedar policies and signed packs.

## Safety & Review Invariants

- All content starts in `Watch` mode during initial validation before promotion (`CONTRIBUTING.md`).
- Never reproduce or paraphrase rules from [security/supply-chain/do-not-read.toml](../../security/supply-chain/do-not-read.toml).
- Provide inert positive (must match) and negative (must not false-positive) fixtures.
- Rules permitting `Block` or containment responses require two independent reviews per repository root `GOVERNANCE.md`.

## Verification Commands

```powershell
cargo test -p grdr-core -p grdr-engine --locked
node scripts/licence-lint.mjs
```

<!-- source: docs/extending/adding-an-agent-manifest.md sha256:0ab44b137a5fe7c2e1afb670d545a2a91a349b60d1745b3ff7e334d22f354ae2 -->
# Adding an Agent Harness Manifest

AI coding agents, CLI harnesses, and MCP clients are described in declarative manifests loaded dynamically by `crates/grdr-agents` rather than hardcoded Rust `enum` variants.

## Steps

1. Inspect [crates/grdr-agents/src/catalogue.rs](../../crates/grdr-agents/src/catalogue.rs) and existing harness manifests to confirm field schema.
2. Add the agent's typed discovery patterns (binary paths, config files, MCP registry locations, and hook dialect identifiers). Never include commands to execute, remote URLs to fetch, or environment mutations in a content manifest (`CONTRIBUTING.md`).
3. Supply at least one benign negative fixture and one positive match fixture with synthetic inputs.
4. Run full verification:

```powershell
cargo test -p grdr-agents --locked
node scripts/check-architecture.mjs
```

<!-- source: docs/extending/README.md sha256:603265a648e1c77cf9d1ec027a769dedc00e3e10cb1fcb669ac80515b548ec33 -->
# Extending Guardrails ADR

Guardrails ADR separates dynamic domain content from compiled core engines. Follow these contributor walkthroughs depending on the extension surface you want to add:

- [Adding an Agent Harness Manifest](adding-an-agent-manifest.md): Declare discovery fingerprints and hook dialects in manifests without touching core enums.
- [Adding a Rule or Policy Pack](adding-a-rule-or-pack.md): Author Cedar policies, signed packs, and benign/adversarial replay fixtures.
- [Adding a Port Adapter](adding-a-port-adapter.md): Implement storage, bus, blob, relational, sandbox, or sensor traits behind `crates/grdr-ports` and verify against `crates/grdr-ports-testkit`.
- [Workspace Crate Map](../crates/README.md): Layering rules (`0..4` and `tool`), `grdr-crypto` cryptographic boundary, and design notes per crate.
- **RFC Process (`rfcs/README.md`):** Open an RFC from `rfcs/0000-template.md` when modifying governed public surfaces or contracts.

<!-- source: docs/training/developer-lab.md sha256:28c788a3125968de203fa2a602721516ba53c407378e578e712c893241fb12a5 -->
# Lab 1: Developer Endpoint Enforcement & Receipt Audit

## Objectives

1. Discover local AI harnesses via `cargo run -p grdr -- scan --json`.
2. Preview (without applying) Claude Code hook installation via `cargo run -p grdr -- hook install --agent claude-code`.
3. Evaluate a sensitive control-file write using `cargo run -p grdr -- check --action file.write --target .claude/settings.json` and confirm `Block` output.
4. Pipe an inert JSON hook event into `cargo run -p grdr-hook` and verify deterministic fail-closed evaluation.
5. Verify hash-chained local receipts using `cargo run -p grdr -- audit verify --json`.

<!-- source: docs/training/operator-lab.md sha256:e778b5011958dd91ff96ac343179a71a5e33be28db53704ef664e0b39a5f4521 -->
# Lab 2: Operator Split-Plane, Recovery Drills, and SaaS Cells

## Objectives

1. Launch `grdr-server` with split Console (`--bind 127.0.0.1:8787`) and Operator (`--operator-bind 127.0.0.1:8788`) bindings and verify startup rejects colliding sockets.
2. Run `cargo run -p grdr-daemon -- --self-test` and confirm OS peer IPC initialization with zero open TCP listeners.
3. Run `cargo run -p grdr -- server preflight --profile embedded --strict --json` and cross-check `upgrade-path.json` and `contracts/upgrade-path.json` against `lifecycle.toml`.
4. Inspect `crates/grdr-saas/tests/saas_ops_tests.rs` and run `cargo test -p grdr-saas --locked` to validate cell splitting (`[0, 4096)`), signed bundle roundtrips (`lake/` + `audit/`), and zero-variance billing reconciliation.
5. Walk through [FLEET-VERIFY.md](../runbooks/FLEET-VERIFY.md) and [RB-01](../runbooks/RB-01-cell-restore-and-dr.md).

<!-- source: docs/training/README.md sha256:bd653db273f5a4f52922cd48298b0a514099f3d7c49796ce13b72fa548fbcd0b -->
# Guardrails ADR Training Labs

Hands-on self-paced labs designed for onboarding solo developers, SRE operators, and external extenders.

- [Developer Lab](developer-lab.md): Build workspace binaries, verify `grdr-hook` fail-closed behavior, run `grdr mcp-proxy`, and verify hash-chained audit logs.
- [Operator Lab](operator-lab.md): Run split Console/Operator servers, execute `grdr server preflight --profile embedded --strict`, run `grdr doctor`, and test SaaS cell portability/reconciliation invariants in `grdr-saas`.

# Public Surfaces and Support Matrix

Generated automatically from `contracts/surfaces.toml` and `contracts/support.toml`.

## Support Policy Bounds

- Release cadence: "monthly"
- Supported minors behind: 2
- Max direct upgrade hop: 2
- Rollback window minors: 1
- Sensor skew tolerance: -2 / +1 minors
- PostgreSQL major tier 1: 18
- Supported Kubernetes versions: ["1.35", "1.36", "1.37"]
